summary: # Quick Start Guide Part 2: How to Make a Maid Costume - Adding an Apron ## Adding Details to the Skirt Next, let's add some details to the skirt part of this set of women's clothes. First, we continue to complete the lower part of the skirt. We found a multidirectional tool in the creation panel tool group. According to the belt we used before, click and draw a skirt panel in the correct order. In the process of drawing, press the left mouse button to create a straight line. Press the control button to create a curve, and release the control button to create a straight line. Finally, click the starting point to complete the closed shape. Adjust the position of the panel in the 3D space. Then switch back to the edit panel tool. Select the line in the front, right-click, choose to align, and edit. After that, adjust the skirt panel left and right. Then arrange the position of the panel in the 2D window. ## Sewing the Skirt Panel Next, use the free powder tool. Start from the front to the side and create the first line. Then sew it in the corresponding position on the belt. After sewing, press the control button to simulate. This panel is newly created, and its particle diameter is set to the default of 20. We will reduce the particle diameter to 8 and the conflict thickness to 1. Then simulate to see its fold distribution. Now we see that the whole panel may be a little wider, so we need to make this panel a little narrower. Use the adjustment panel tool to select the whole panel, then drag the selection frame of the selected panel to shrink it. After shrinking, don't forget to manually adjust the position of the panel in the 3D space to prevent it from intersecting with other panels. ## Adjusting the Seam Next, use the edit powder line tool (the express key is B) to adjust the position of the seam here on the belt. Press the control button to start the simulation. Because of the previous creation angle, we will directly use the straight point. If we add the edge to it directly, this straight point will not be very smooth. We found the deep and smooth curve tool in the edit powder tool group. Click and drag this point to form an angle, ensuring this curve is very smooth. When we turn the view to the side, we will see some bones in the front. If you want to flatten this part of the bone, we need to remove this part of the bone. Select the point in the front and drag it down to remove a small part of the panel in the middle. Then simulate to ensure the middle is flat. ## Activating and Simulating the Panels Next, we activate the belt of the seam. Because of the same frozen panel mentioned before, if you adjust the panel of the seam, it may cause an intersection with other panels due to the re-arrangement of the grid. So, we reduce the particle diameter of the belt panel and set its level to 1, allowing it to pass through the outer part of the other panels. After the simulation is stable, we return the level to 0, activate the skirt part of the skirt, and simulate it together. Here, we untangle the skirt panel and simulate it together to prevent instability when the whole is untangled. After the simulation is stable, we can choose to hide the outer panel by pressing Shift + Q. ## Final Adjustments and Merging Panels Now, activate the inner skirt and simulate it together. Once the simulation is stable, we can freeze all the panels. Since we are going to increase the edge of the skirt panel later, we activate the skirt panel first. Use the editor panel tool to select the three edges simultaneously, then go to the attribute editor to check the total length of their 2D line. Using the rectangle tool, create a single machine in the 2D window. Ensure the width is slightly more than the measurement value just obtained. Next, use the free-format tool to merge the sides of the two panels together. When using the free-format tool, even if there is a break in the middle, it can still be selected. Select these two edge panels simultaneously, right-click, and add them to the side. After adding, if they conflict with the panel inside, set its level to 1 in the attribute editor, allowing it to simulate and stabilize. Once stable, return the level to 0 to prevent interruptions from other errors. ## Dealing with Bulges and Final Touches Next, activate the belt panel related to them and simulate together. After the simulation, we see that the bulge in the waist is unresolved, indicating it's not related to the belt but to other panels. So we activate the other panels and simulate again. After the simulation, we ensure that it appears flat. Once frozen, we can make the edges more pronounced. Select the panel in the 2D window, loosen the panel, and make it wider. This adjustment effectively increases the length of the panel. After adding, select to add to the side. Once the simulation is opened, the edge effect emerges. After achieving a stable simulation effect, we will add the line between them. We choose to add after because we just used the function of adding to the side. If we create the line first, it may affect our use of the add function. Now, switch to the free line tool. For the side of the belt close to the edge, smear on the belt while locating the mouse on the line to find it according to the reference instructions. From the end of it, continue to sew to the side. After adjusting the length, we use the adjustment panel tool to select the two side panels and reduce their particle diameter to 5, along with the conflict thickness to 1. ## Simulation and Merging Final Panels Since these two panels are not very large, reducing their particle diameter to 5 is acceptable. Then select all panels (Ctrl + A), activate them, and press the control key to simulate. After the simulation effect is satisfactory, reduce all particle diameters to 5 and press the control key to simulate again. Once the overall shape meets your satisfaction, we will start merging the panels. First, switch to the editor panel tool to select the lines. According to the blue reference point in the 3D window, find the two lines we want to merge. When selecting simultaneously, right-click and choose merge. Because it is a left and right symmetrical panel, when you choose one of them, the other line will automatically be selected. Thus, you can right-click to choose merge, and it will also merge correctly. If there is no symmetry, you need to select both lines simultaneously to merge them together. These left and right symmetrical panels, after merging along a line, will still be symmetrical. In the adjustment process, it may cause the left and right of the panel to become asymmetrical. For instance, here is the sleeve; we can select one of the sleeves and delete it by pressing the delete button. After deleting, use the adjustment panel tool to select the two panels of the sleeve and press Ctrl + D to create a symmetrical panel. Since the shape has been adjusted previously, the symmetrical panel we created will also be adjusted and automatically generated. We just need to ensure it is placed correctly. ## Finalizing the Outfit If the current panel shape is not as desired, we can freeze other panels first. For example, if I want to modify this sound, I will freeze all other panels and find the fabric of this top. Increase the strength of its fineliner and raise the tension on the feet to create more pronounced creases. After opening the model, you will see the entire outfit looks tight because of its stretching performance, which can worsen and lead to more obvious creases. Finally, let's address the chest pull effect. First, we choose the top line, right-click, and select the internal line. Then, choose the new internal line and opt to cut and sew. After cutting, the panel is no longer symmetrical, but that’s okay. We use the adjustment panel tool, double-click the center to open the center point. This way, our adjustments are based on the center point. Since this panel has widened, the lines that are in harmony with it have not been widened, causing creases to pile up in the front. We just need to change the fabric color. That completes our final effect. See you in the next video! Bye bye!
